title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 31 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 31 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 31 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 31.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 31, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.explanation: The destruction of images is mentioned first in the chapter as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:1.

questions.question: Who appointed the courses of the priests and Levites?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah appointed the courses of the priests and the Levites as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:2.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the priests and Levites according to their courses?
questions.explanation: The priests and Levites were appointed for burnt offerings and peace offerings, as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:2.

questions.question: What portion did Hezekiah appoint for burnt offerings?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah appointed the king's portion of his substance for burnt offerings as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:3.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah command the people in Jerusalem to give?
options: Portion for the priests and Levites
questions.correctAnswer: Portion for the priests and Levites
questions.explanation: Hezekiah commanded the people to give the portion of the priests and the Levites as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 31:4.

questions.question: What did the children of Israel bring in abundance after the commandment?
options: Firstfruits of corn, wine, and oil
questions.correctAnswer: Firstfruits of corn, wine, and oil
questions.explanation: The children of Israel brought in abundance the firstfruits of corn, wine, and oil as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:5.

questions.question: What additional offerings did the children of Israel bring?
questions.explanation: They brought in the tithe of oxen and sheep as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 31:6.

questions.question: In which month did they begin to lay the foundation of the heaps?
questions.explanation: They began to lay the foundation of the heaps in the third month as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:7.

questions.question: In which month did they finish laying the heaps?
questions.explanation: They finished laying the heaps in the seventh month as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 31:7.

questions.question: Did Hezekiah encourage the people to support the priests and Levites?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah commanded the people to give the portion of the priests and Levites to encourage them in the law of the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:4.

questions.question: Did the children of Israel bring the tithe abundantly?
questions.explanation: The children of Israel brought in abundantly the tithe of all things, as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:5.

questions.question: True or False: Hezekiah instructed the people to destroy all high places in Judah.
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's actions resulted in the destruction of high places as detailed in 2 Chronicles 31:1.

questions.question: True or False: The heaps were finished in the eighth month.
questions.explanation: The heaps were finished in the seventh month, as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:7.

questions.question: True or False: Only the Levites received a portion from the people.
questions.explanation: Both priests and Levites received a portion according to 2 Chronicles 31:4.

questions.question: True or False: Hezekiah appointed the courses of the prophets.
questions.explanation: Hezekiah appointed the courses of the priests and the Levites, not prophets, as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:2.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 31 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 31 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah and the princes do when they saw the heaps?
options: They blessed the LORD and his people Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: They blessed the LORD and his people Israel.
questions.explanation: Hezekiah and the princes blessed the LORD and his people Israel when they saw the heaps, as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:8.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 31:10 promise will happen if the people bring their offerings into the house of the LORD?
options: They will have enough to eat and leave plenty.
questions.correctAnswer: They will have enough to eat and leave plenty.
questions.explanation: Azariah states that since the people began to bring offerings, they have had enough to eat and left plenty, indicating divine blessing, as seen in 2 Chronicles 31:10.

questions.question: Who was the ruler over the offerings and the tithes in the house of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Cononiah the Levite was the ruler over the offerings and tithes as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:12.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 31:4 command the people to do for the priests and Levites?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah commanded the people to give the portion of the priests and Levites to encourage them in the law of the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:4.

questions.question: How did the children of Israel respond to the commandment regarding offerings?
questions.explanation: The children of Israel brought in abundance the firstfruits and tithes as soon as the commandment came, as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:5.

questions.question: Who was the chief priest that answered Hezekiah's question about the heaps?
questions.explanation: Azariah the chief priest of the house of Zadok answered Hezekiah concerning the heaps, as noted in 2 Chronicles 31:10.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah command to be prepared in the house of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah commanded to prepare chambers in the house of the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:11.

questions.question: What was Kore's role in the offerings?
questions.explanation: Kore the son of Imnah was the porter toward the east, overseeing the freewill offerings of God, as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:14.

questions.question: How did the people of Judah respond to the command regarding the tithe?
questions.explanation: The people of Judah brought the tithe of oxen and sheep and laid them by heaps, as noted in 2 Chronicles 31:6.

questions.question: What was the time frame for laying the foundation of the heaps?
questions.explanation: In the third month, they began to lay the foundation of the heaps and finished them in the seventh month, as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:7.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of the people bringing their offerings?
options: To gain favor with the king
To support the priests and Levites
questions.correctAnswer: To support the priests and Levites
questions.explanation: The people's offerings were intended to encourage the priests and Levites in their service to the law of the LORD, as indicated in 2 Chronicles 31:4.

questions.question: The people of Israel were encouraged to bring their offerings for what reason?
questions.explanation: The command was for the people to give portions to the priests and Levites to encourage them in the law of the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:4.

questions.question: Is it true that Hezekiah questioned the priests concerning the heaps?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah questioned the priests and Levites concerning the heaps, as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:9.

questions.question: Is it true that the heaps were a result of the people ignoring offerings?
questions.explanation: The heaps were a result of the people's abundant offerings, not from ignoring them, as indicated in 2 Chronicles 31:10.

questions.question: Is it true that the priests were in charge of preparing the chambers in the house of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah commanded the preparation of chambers, which indicates he and the princes were in charge, as stated in 2 Chronicles 31:11.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 31 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 31.

questions.question: Who were mentioned next to Eden in their set office in the cities of the priests?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is found in 2 Chronicles 31:15, which lists Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah in their set office.

questions.question: What age range is specified for males in the genealogy mentioned in 2 Chronicles 31:16?
options: From three years old and upward
From twenty years old and upward
From one year old and upward
From fifteen years old and upward
questions.correctAnswer: From three years old and upward
questions.explanation: According to 2 Chronicles 31:16, the genealogy of males is from three years old and upward.

questions.question: What was required of the Levites according to their courses as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 31:17?
options: To give portions to the priests
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 31:18 states that the Levites sanctified themselves in holiness in their set office.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah do throughout all Judah as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 31:20?
options: He wrought that which was good and right
He commanded the people to give offerings
questions.correctAnswer: He wrought that which was good and right
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 31:20, it is noted that Hezekiah wrought that which was good and right and truth before the LORD.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah do with all his heart according to 2 Chronicles 31:21?
options: He led the people in worship
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 31:21 indicates that Hezekiah sought his God with all his heart.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 31:19, who were expressed by name to give portions to the priests?
questions.explanation: The verse 2 Chronicles 31:19 specifically mentions the sons of Aaron as those who were expressed by name to give portions to the priests.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Hezekiah' in 2 Chronicles 31:20 mean?
questions.explanation: The name 'Hezekiah' in Hebrew means 'God strengthens', which reflects his role as a reformer in Judah.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in the phrase 'to give to their brethren by courses' in 2 Chronicles 31:15?
questions.explanation: The phrase reflects parallelism as it contrasts the roles of two groups giving to their brethren.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of priestly service in 2 Chronicles 31:20?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 2:9 speaks of believers as a royal priesthood, echoing the theme of priestly service found in 2 Chronicles 31:20.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the theme of offering and tithing as seen in 2 Chronicles 31:5?
questions.explanation: Malachi 3:10 discusses bringing tithes and offerings into the storehouse, fulfilling the theme in 2 Chronicles 31:5.

questions.question: What comes before 2 Chronicles 31:15?
questions.explanation: The verse immediately before 2 Chronicles 31:15 discusses the appointment of the courses of the priests and Levites.

questions.question: What does the term 'sanctified' in 2 Chronicles 31:18 imply about the Levites' status?
options: They were set apart for service
questions.correctAnswer: They were set apart for service
questions.explanation: The term 'sanctified' in this context indicates that the Levites were set apart for their holy service as noted in 2 Chronicles 31:18.

questions.question: Hezekiah's reforms were characterized by what type of dedication according to 2 Chronicles 31:21?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 31:21 emphasizes that Hezekiah did every work with all his heart, highlighting his genuine dedication.

questions.question: Is it true that all Israel returned to their possessions after the reforms of Hezekiah according to 2 Chronicles 31:1?
questions.explanation: This is true as 2 Chronicles 31:1 states that all Israel returned to their possessions after the reforms were completed.

questions.question: Is it false that Hezekiah commanded the people to disregard the portion for the priests and Levites?
questions.explanation: This is false because, according to 2 Chronicles 31:4, Hezekiah commanded the people to give the portion of the priests and Levites.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 31 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 31 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 31:3 teach about God's provision and covenantal worship?
options: God provides a lawful system for continual worship through appointed offerings
Worship is optional and based on personal preference
The king's wealth is separate from religious duties
Offerings are only required during harvest festivals
questions.correctAnswer: God provides a lawful system for continual worship through appointed offerings
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 31:3 shows Hezekiah appointing the king's portion for regular burnt offerings as written in the law, indicating God’s provision for continual covenant worship.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification and communal holiness does 2 Chronicles 31:18 teach?
options: Sanctification involves the entire congregation setting themselves apart in holiness
Only priests are required to live holy lives
Holiness is a private matter unrelated to community
Sanctification applies only during temple service
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves the entire congregation setting themselves apart in holiness
questions.explanation: Verse 18 highlights that all the congregation, including families, sanctified themselves in holiness by their set office, emphasizing communal sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning stewardship and faithfulness does 2 Chronicles 31:5 teach?
options: Faithful giving of firstfruits and tithes is a joyful response to God's blessings
Giving is an obligatory burden for the people
Tithing is only symbolic without practical value
Offerings should be minimal to avoid hardship
questions.correctAnswer: Faithful giving of firstfruits and tithes is a joyful response to God's blessings
questions.explanation: The abundance of firstfruits and tithes brought by the people in verse 5 indicates faithful, joyful stewardship in response to God's provision.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 31:10 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 states the LORD hath blessed his people, showing God's attribute of blessing in response to obedience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 31:21 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah prospered because he sought God with all his heart and obeyed His law, demonstrating God's faithfulness to those who earnestly seek Him (verse 21).

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 31:1–2 connect to the theme of covenant renewal seen throughout Scripture?
options: It illustrates the removal of idolatry as a prerequisite for covenant restoration
It shows God's covenant is unconditional regardless of Israel's actions
It emphasizes that physical destruction of idols is sufficient for salvation
It reveals that only the Levites are responsible for covenant faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the removal of idolatry as a prerequisite for covenant restoration
questions.explanation: Verses 1–2 depict Israel destroying idols and organizing priestly service, reflecting covenant renewal themes like in Deuteronomy 30:6 where circumcision of the heart precedes restoration.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 31:11–13 prepare the redemptive-historical theme of priestly mediation seen in the New Testament?
options: It shows the organized and faithful administration of offerings, foreshadowing Christ as the High Priest
It reveals that human priests have ultimate authority apart from God
It implies that ritual sacrifices are unnecessary
It focuses only on political governance, unrelated to mediation
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the organized and faithful administration of offerings, foreshadowing Christ as the High Priest
questions.explanation: The careful preparation of chambers and oversight of offerings in verses 11–13 reflect priestly mediation, pointing typologically to Christ’s perfect priesthood (Hebrews 7).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 6 and 19 teach about the role of tithes and genealogies in maintaining covenant community?
options: Tithes are given systematically and genealogies ensure proper distribution among covenant priests and Levites
Genealogies are irrelevant to worship practices
Tithes can be given randomly without structure
Only Levites without genealogy receive tithes
questions.correctAnswer: Tithes are given systematically and genealogies ensure proper distribution among covenant priests and Levites
questions.explanation: Verse 6 mentions tithes of oxen and sheep consecrated to God, and verse 19 describes named priests in cities who distribute portions according to genealogies, showing systematic stewardship.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 15 and 16 teach about God's provision and the inclusion of all ages in covenant service?
options: God’s provision is distributed according to appointed courses, including males from age three upwards, ensuring all generations participate in service
Only adult males are entitled to receive portions
Women are excluded from covenant provision
Provision is given randomly without order
questions.correctAnswer: God’s provision is distributed according to appointed courses, including males from age three upwards, ensuring all generations participate in service
questions.explanation: Verses 15–16 describe distribution to priests and Levites by courses, with daily portions for males from three years old and upward, showing inclusive provision in covenant service.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 4 and 20 teach about leadership and obedience in covenant renewal?
options: Godly leadership commands obedience that results in doing what is good, right, and true before the LORD
Leadership is irrelevant to covenant obedience
Obedience depends solely on popular opinion
Covenant renewal happens without any human initiative
questions.correctAnswer: Godly leadership commands obedience that results in doing what is good, right, and true before the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 4 shows Hezekiah commanding support for priests, and verse 20 affirms Hezekiah’s works as good and right before God, demonstrating leadership’s role in covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Chronicles 31:5–10 teaches that God's blessing is merely a result of material prosperity without spiritual significance. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God blesses obedience, which includes faithful giving, resulting in material provision and spiritual encouragement
Material prosperity is the only sign of God's favor
Blessings are unrelated to human obedience or giving
The passage encourages greed for wealth as divine blessing
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses obedience, which includes faithful giving, resulting in material provision and spiritual encouragement
questions.explanation: Verses 5–10 show the people’s abundant offerings and the priests’ statement that the LORD has blessed his people, linking blessing to faithful obedience and worship.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 31:12 teach about the role of appointed rulers in temple service?
options: God ordains leaders to oversee faithful administration of offerings and dedicated things
Temple service is chaotic without human leadership
Rulers have no authority in religious matters
Offering distribution is left to chance
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains leaders to oversee faithful administration of offerings and dedicated things
questions.explanation: Verse 12 describes Cononiah and Shimei as rulers appointed to oversee offerings, showing God’s design for orderly leadership in worship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 31:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: When Hezekiah and the princes saw the heaps of offerings, they blessed the LORD and His people, reflecting God’s attribute of eliciting grateful worship (verse 8).

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 31:14–15 illustrate theological principles about God’s provision and distribution in worship?
options: God’s provision is entrusted to appointed Levites who distribute offerings orderly to maintain covenantal worship
Offerings are hoarded by priests without distribution
Distribution occurs without regard to family or service
Provision is only for the wealthy priests
questions.correctAnswer: God’s provision is entrusted to appointed Levites who distribute offerings orderly to maintain covenantal worship
questions.explanation: Verses 14–15 describe Kore and others distributing the freewill offerings and portions by courses, reflecting orderly stewardship in covenant worship.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 31:17 and 31:19 teach about the importance of genealogical order in Levite and priestly ministry?
options: Genealogical order ensures proper service and distribution among priests and Levites, maintaining covenant purity
Genealogy is irrelevant to ministry roles
Priests and Levites serve interchangeably without order
Genealogical records are only for civil purposes
questions.correctAnswer: Genealogical order ensures proper service and distribution among priests and Levites, maintaining covenant purity
questions.explanation: Verse 17 specifies priests and Levites serve according to genealogies and courses, and verse 19 shows portions given to those reckoned by genealogies, emphasizing order and purity.
